items.title: Khaitan & Co acts on Matel ₹130 crore Series B fundraise
items.summary: Matel Motion and Energy Solutions Private Limited has raised ₹130 crore from a Series B fundraise led by by UC Impower, with Catamaran joining as a new investor and Transition VC continuing its support as an existing investor. Khaitan & Co advised Matel on this fundraise. The transaction team consisted of Bhavik Narsana (Partner), Shweta Dwivedi (Consultant), Pragya Mishra (Associate) and Sakshi Mehta (Associate). Matel is an Indian technology company which designs and manufactures energy-efficient motors, motor controllers and integrated powertrains for automotive and industrial applications, including electric vehicles, pumping and cooling systems. The new capital will be allocated to increase the company's manufacturing capacity, enhance research and development efforts, speed up the creation of new products, and hire additional engineering and production personnel. items.title: Introducing India’s first Court Downtime Tracker
items.summary: Is it just me? She wonders, staring at her screen. The court website has failed her yet again. She frantically refreshes, reboots, switches browsers - nothing works. A colleague in the corner says, "It's working fine for me." The mystery never stops. This isn't a one-off. It's just one example of the countless times each week that a court website fails to load for the average litigator, litigant, journalist, or legal researcher. Things get worse as you move down the judicial hierarchy. Court websites - a basic tool that facilitates access to justice in the digital age - are riddled with poor functionality, clunky interfaces, missing orders, mangled judge names, algebraic captchas and more. On this August 15th, we make our contribution to easing access to justice - independence from the endless cycle of refresh, reboot, recheck. Our Court Downtime Tracker , a joint initiative by the CourtsDaily team and Bar & Bench , will now host a live, ticking tracker that continually monitors and records court websites across forums and shows their uptime status in real time. .responsive-iframe-courtsdaily { width: 100%; height: 540px; /* Mobile default */ border: 0; } @media (min-width: 768px)

items.title: Nip it in the bud: Bombay High Court calls for aggressive sterilisation of stray dogs
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Friday suggested that the Maharashtra government aggressively implement the Animal Birth Control (ABC) programme to halt the growth of stray dog population. A division bench of acting Chief Justice Ravindra V Ghuge and Justice Gautam A Ankhad emphasised that prioritising sterilisation of adult dogs over managing expanding numbers would naturally address the issue. Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad The bench observed that halting the growth of the stray dog population is key to resolving the broader crisis. “Your administration must realise one thing, that if you implement that ABC program aggressively, there will be no growth of dogs (stray). Every dog which is sterilised through the ABC program, there can be no procreation,” ACJ Ghuge said. He emphasised that instead of trying to catch hold of the growing number of dogs, the State could catch adult dogs and sterilise them. “If there is no birth of puppies later, then you are nipping the disease in the bud. items.title: Protect interests of students: Supreme Court asks CBSE to address OSM evaluation issues
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday asked the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to explore ways to protect the interests of students facing difficulties in entrance-based admissions due to their scores under the Board’s new On-Screen Marking (OSM) system for evaluating answer sheets. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told that some students had cleared their CBSE examinations and had subsequently appeared for entrance examinations for other courses. However, they had not secured the minimum marks required for admission because of their CBSE scores, and some of the courses had already commenced. The plea linked the lesser marks/ scores to the irregularities in OSM evaluation system. The Bench then asked CBSE to examine the issue and find out how the interests of such students could be protected. "Please find out how can you protect their interest," the Court said before adjourning the matter. items.title: Lawyers' instinct to question authority not merely a legacy of freedom struggle, relevant even today: CJI Surya Kant
items.summary: Legal profession's instinct to test any exercise of authority against the values of justice, fairness and rule of law is not merely a legacy of India's freedom movement but remains relevant today, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said on Saturday. He was delivering the chief guest's address at the Supreme Court Bar Association's Independence Day function on the Supreme Court lawns. "I believe that instinct to examine the exercise of authority in any form or manner against the values of justice, fairness, and rule of law is not just a legacy of the freedom movement. It remains relevant to us even today, and reminds us of the foundational Constitutional rights that we have inherited, which enable us to protect the civil liberties of individuals," the CJI said. He said lawyers are trained to look beyond the mere existence of a rule and ask whether the exercise of power was consistent with the principles meant to justify it. This, he said, was the question that had confronted British colonial rule - if a government claims to rule through law, can that law deny liberty, equality and dignity to the people it governs. items.title: Delhi HC asks Centre, CBFC, film producers to decide on adding accessibility features in cinema, OTT for disabled
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB), Central Board Of Film Certification (CBFC), Mythri Movie Makers and other relevant stakeholders to deliberate upon adding accessibility features in films released in cinema and over-the-top (OTT) platforms for disabled audience [ Rahul Bajaj vs. Mythri Movie Makers And Ors ]. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma passed the directions on August 10 while hearing a petition filed by disability rights activist and lawyer Rahul Bajaj. "This Court considers it appropriate to afford an opportunity to all concerned stakeholders to deliberate upon the issue and explore a mutually acceptable resolution. Accordingly, a joint meeting of all stakeholders, including the petitioner and the respondents, shall be convened within a period of one week from today to consider the broader concerns regarding accessibility of films raised by the petitioner," the order said. The Court directed the stakeholders to reach a workable resolution in this regard within two weeks. [ Kamakhya Das v. State of Maharashtra & Ors. ]. Justice Prafulla Khubalkar noted that the electronic devices belonging the accused Kamakhya Das were already seized and custodial interrogation would not be necessary at this stage. Hence, the judge granted bail to Das while asking him cooperate with the ongoing investigation. "Considering the nature of the allegations and the fact that the mobile phone and laptop of the applicant are already seized, at this stage, custodial interrogation need not be insisted upon. Hence, the interim protection granted by the trial court needs to be continued further, subject to certain conditions," the judge held. Das was directed to attend the concerned police station on August 19 and 24 between 10 am to 2 pm. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday sought the Central government’s response to a plea seeking implementation of the top court's directions on the mandatory reporting of Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse Material (CSEAM) by social media intermediaries. [ Just Rights for Children Alliance & Anr. v. S. Harish & Ors] The plea also said there should be criminal action against intermediaries that fail to report CSEAM. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and Vinod Chandran issued notice to the government on the plea. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The plea was filed by Just Rights for Children Alliance (JRCA) seeking implementation of the Supreme Court’s September 2024 judgment , which held that social media intermediaries are mandatorily required to report offences relating to CSEAM to the concerned police authorities under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act) and the rules framed under it. The Court had also held that an intermediary cannot claim protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000 unless it exercises due diligence and complies with its obligations under the POCSO Act and Rules. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday refused to pass any interim orders on a plea filed by Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) to stop a private television channel from broadcasting or rebroadcasting Gurbani (sacred hymns and scriptures of Sikhism) from the Golden Temple. SGPC and a channel named PTC approached the High Court against Galactic Television and Communications alleging copyright infringement. SGPC – the apex body entrusted with managing the Golden Temple (Sri Harmandir Sahib) – argued that they hold the copyright in the broadcast of the Gurbani from the Golden Temple. It stated that Galactic Television, by broadcasting the same, although with a 10-second delay, is violating their rights. At present, the Gurbani from the Golden Temple is broadcast on SGPC’s YouTube channel and on PTC. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani today gave a prima facie opinion that the Guru Granth Sahib is a literary work and that if its broadcast by SGPC is used for a genuine religious ceremony without resorting to commercialisation, it may not amount to copyright infringement. “It is a literary cum musical work. items.title: Karnataka has released enough water: Supreme Court to Tamil Nadu in Cauvery water dispute
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday remarked that the State of Tamil Nadu appeared to be receiving more water from the Cauvery River in Karnataka than its allocated share. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta made the observation while hearing the Tamil Nadu government's plea seeking directions for immediate release of its due share of Cauvery water. The TN government has alleged that the State is not receiving its allocated share from Karnataka despite facing a rain-deficient year. items.title: Madras High Court grants anti-piracy injunction in favour of Aamir Khan-produced Batwara 1947
items.summary: The Madras High Court has granted an interim injunction to Aamir Khan Productions to prevent the unauthorised online and cable distribution of its recently released film Batwara 1947 . [Aamir Khan Production Vs BSNL] By way of an order passed on August 14, Justice K Surender directed internet service providers to block websites hosting pirated copies of the film. The Court passed the direction after observing that the production house was likely to suffer irreversible injury unless the unlawful broadcast of the film was prevented. “ In matter of this nature, it is likely that irreversible injury will occur, unless unlawful broadcast is prevented ,” the Court said while granting interim injunction. The Court also issued notice to the respondents (mobile and internet service providers) and sought their responses. The injunction will remain in force until September 11, when the matter will next be heard. Batwara 1947 , directed by Rajkumar Santoshi and starring Sunny Deol, Preity Zinta and Shabana Azmi, was released theatrically on August 14. NTPC Limited ]. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe criticised RIL for repeatedly raising objections that prevented the commercial suit from proceeding beyond the evidence stage. “ There is no dearth of financial resources, no obligation to aid and assist the court to cope with pending backlog of cases, perhaps it is lucrative for RIL to raise some objection or the other at every stage and when the trial court rejects it, the appellate and special leave jurisdictions open up ,” the Court said. The facts of the case would reveal that Reliance Industries appeared to have unlimited power to litigate and obstruct the progress of the case, the Bench stated. “ This litigation has multiple seasons laden with many episodes ,” the judgment added. items.title: Husband called wife barren, wife called husband impotent: What Allahabad HC held
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently observed that addressing a wife as “barren woman” may not constitute cruelty under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) when there is exchange of “filthy verbal blows” from both sides. Justice Indrajeet Shukla was dealing with a man’s petition challenging a Lucknow court order summoning him in a complaint filed by his wife over alleged cruelty, dowry demand and intentional insult. “In the case in hand, the entire version of complainant if tested on the touchstone of legal requirements, for even prima facie constituting the offence of cruelty, the address as ‘barren woman’ could not be termed as cruelty, particularly when there are exchange of filthy verbal blows from both the sides,” the Court said. items.title: Karnataka High Court permits Hindu Jagarana Vedike’s Mysuru torchlight procession on Independence Day eve
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Friday permitted the Hindu Jagarana Vedike to conduct its ‘Akhanda Bharata Sankalpa Dina’ torchlight procession in Mysuru on the eve of Independence Day [ Hindu Jagrana Vedike & another vs The Commissioner of Police & another ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj , however, made it clear that the procession's organisers would be held responsible if any untoward incident takes place during the march. The Court has directed the police to provide necessary security for the procession from RMC Ganesha Temple to Dodda Gadiyara Circle, which will commence at 5:30 PM and conclude at 7:30 PM on August 14. The Court passed the order after rejecting the State's argument that there is possibility of unlawful incidents arising during the march since some of the programme's organisers had a history of anti-social activities and have criminal cases pending against them. The Court opined that this cannot be a ground to prevent them from participating in Independence Day celebrations. items.title: Supreme Court quashes FIRs against Samay Raina, 4 other comedians over remarks about disabled persons
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday quashed criminal cases filed against YouTuber-comedian Samay Raina and four other comedians over insensitive remarks made on the show India's Got Latent about persons with disabilities. A Bench Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order. Apart from Raina, the others who have been given relief in connection with this case are Vipul Goyal, Balraj Paramjeet Singh Ghai, Sonali Thakkar alias Sonali Aditya Desai, and Nishant Jagdish Tanwar. The Court today appreciated the efforts made by Raina, Goyal, Ghai, Thakkar and Tanwar to organise shows for the benefit of persons with disabilities. " Once there are genuine efforts positive results are bound to be there. They are very bright youngsters. If they have started working in positive direction, there will be positive output," the Bench said. The Court proceeded to quash criminal cases filed against them over insensitve remarks against disabled persons.
